Team / Alex — ran a quick sizing pass against their sample and sketched two candidate pools. Summary first, details below and attached "spectra_kv_sim.xlsx" with per-token KV curves.

Summary (approx):
- Model residency: Llama-3-70B (baseline FP16 weights + activations) typically needs ~160–180 GB of GPU RAM to host model state with operational headroom. At FP16 that implies multi-GPU model-parallel (2x H100-80GB with sharded weights) or a single 80GB with weight offload — not ideal for latency.
- Quantized option: 4-bit weight quant (Q4 variants) reduces on-device weight size ~3.5x vs FP16. That lets Llama-3-70B weights fit into a single H100-80GB instance (weights ~45–55 GB) leaving room for KV and activations. Latency penalty for decode is small (~5–12% depending on kernel maturity).
- KV cache sizing: from our empirical sims, FP16 KV uses ~0.9 GB per 1k tokens for L3-70B. Thus: 16k ~=14.4GB, 32k ~=28.8GB, 64k ~=57.6GB (per concurrent session). With ~60% cache reuse, effective steady-state KV memory demand drops by similar factor for conversational hotspots.
- Offload strategy: use NVMe-backed KV offload for cold tails (cheap storage, higher tail latency). Keep hot prefixes in-GPU and tune eviction to target p95. Offload reduces required GPU RAM but increases variance in p95 latency for long-context rare calls.

Recommended Dedicated pool sizes (to hit p50 <250ms, p95 <600ms at 120rps sustained):
- Conservative (FP16, minimal quant): 18 H100-80GB GPUs configured across model-parallel sets for L3-70B (effectively ~9 model instances with autoscale headroom). This prioritizes latency and avoids offload for 32k contexts.
- Cost-optimized (Q4 weights + KV offload): 10 H100-80GB GPUs with aggressive packing and a small NVMe cluster for KV offload; apply per-route caching to keep most sessions in GPU memory. Expected cost delta: ~45–55% lower infra cost vs conservative but p95 of 64k cold calls may exceed their p95 target unless we increase hot-memory retention.

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Canary plan: start with 2% of traffic on quantized instances for 2 weeks, monitor hallucination/regression via eval prompts and quality telemetry.
- Latency vs quant: Q4 introduces slight decode overhead; but our optimized kernels shrink the throughput delta. If Spectra demands strict p95 across all 64k calls, we must keep a small pool of FP16 instances for fallback (recommended: 2–3 model-parallel FP16 nodes).
- Sizing formula (high level): GPU_resident_memory = Quantized_weight_size + KV_hot + Activation_headroom + OS/runtime overhead. KV_hot ~= tokens_hot * kv_bytes_per_token (we measured ~0.9GB per 1k tokens in FP16 for L3-70B).

I attached the sim; Marissa, can you convert these into a pricing ballpark for their procurement doc? If Alex is comfortable, we’ll propose a pilot: 6 Dedicated GPUs (quantized) for 30 days with telemetry and a canary mix, then expand to full pool.

— Ben
